name: B200
summary: Kernels are written on the development GPU and graded on an NVIDIA B200. Only bytes that compile and run on the graded machine count.

software.note: The board's evaluation image (SOL-ExecBench docker/Dockerfile). A local reading taken with other versions is a reading from another stack: useful, not equal.

evaluation.timer: span from the first to the last kernel of one call (CUPTI), host-side gaps between kernels included
evaluation.outputs: pre-allocated by the harness and passed after the inputs (DPS)
evaluation.each_solution_in: a fresh subprocess, compiled from scratch
evaluation.note: Every evaluation recompiles: the cold start (imports plus all compilation) must stay well inside a minute.

submission.track_format: one directory per kernel, each holding a single submission.py
submission.entry: top-level run(*args); the contract is argument order and count, names are not enforced; outputs arrive pre-allocated last
track_languages: python (pytorch / triton / cute dsl / cuda compiled at run time)
submission.embedded_source: CUDA C++ is allowed when embedded in submission.py and built at run time (torch.utils.cpp_extension); no separate .cu in a track submission
prohibited: hidden CUDA streams outside the timed path
returning a lazy proxy instead of a real tensor
degenerate output (NaN / inf / zeros) that the reference does not produce

rules.text: The kernel is graded on NVIDIA B200 (CC 10.0, sm_100a, 148 SMs, 8 TB/s, clocks locked at 1500 / 3996 MHz, cold L2 on every call).
Do not use any feature that CC 10.0 lacks. Never name an architecture in the code: derive it from the device at run time.
Never hard-code the SM count: query it (FK_TARGET_SMS overrides it when set).
Dense FP4 throughput and SFU throughput are higher on the development GPU: timings of kernels bound by them are optimistic here.
The submission is one submission.py with a top-level run(*args); arguments are positional (inputs, then pre-allocated outputs).

Allowed libraries: PyTorch operators, Triton, CuTe DSL, cuBLAS / cuDNN through torch, CUTLASS headers; CUDA C++ only inline (compiled at run time through torch.utils.cpp_extension). Everything else must be embedded as source.
Compilation happens on every evaluation: keep it well inside a minute, cache nothing outside the process.
Leave global state as you found it (restore any torch.backends flag you change inside run).

The L2 cache is flushed before every timed call, the inputs are cloned and land at a new address on every call: never rely on cache residency across calls or on pointer identity. Minimise the bytes you move; fuse what would otherwise be separate kernels.
The stopwatch is the span from the first to the last kernel of one call: host-side gaps between kernels count. Keep the Python between launches minimal, or launch everything from one kernel.
Outputs are pre-allocated: write into them directly, do not allocate a result and copy it over.
Every evaluation compiles from scratch. Keep the cold start (import + all compilation) far below two minutes; prefer a table of per-shape constants over run-time autotuning.

codegen.note: The card built by `forge run` compiles for the development machine (task.toml dev_arch, exported as CUTE_DSL_ARCH / FK_CUDA_ARCH). A submission does neither: it derives the gencode from torch.cuda.get_device_capability() and reads FK_TARGET_SMS only when it is set.
